'''''Festuca salzmannii''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Poaceae]] (grasses), [[Native species|native]] to the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] from Spain to Cyprus, and to Turkey.<ref name=POWO_403463-1/> It has been placed in the genus '''''Narduroides''''' as the sole species '''''Narduroides salzmannii'''''.

==Description==
''Festuca salzmannii'' is an annual with slender, erect stems up to {{Cvt|40|cm|ftin|0}} tall that are relatively rigid. The [[inflorescence]] can be up to {{Cvt|23|cm|in|0}} long, usually unbranched, but rarely with a few branches. Individual spikelets have 4–6 florets and are typically {{Cvt|4|–|7|mm|in|1}} long. The ripe grains are {{Cvt|1|–|1.8|mm|in|2}} long.<ref name=Tuti80p157/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Pierre Edmond Boissier]] in 1844 as ''Nardurus salzmannii''.<!--ref name=IPNI_403463-1/--> In 1851, Boissier transferred it to the genus ''[[Festuca]]''.<ref name=POWO_403463-1/> In 1913, [[Georges Rouy]] placed it as the sole species in the genus ''Narduroides''.<ref name=RouyFoucCamu13/> {{As of|2024|November}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] regarded ''Narduroides'' as a [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of ''Festuca''.<ref name=POWO_18560-1/>

==Distribution==
''Festuca salzmannii'' is native to [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Morocco]], [[Algeria]], [[Libya]], [[Greece]], the [[Aegean Sea|East Aegean islands]], [[Cyprus]], and [[Turkey]].<ref name=POWO_403463-1/>
